expectations.text: Preserves 18 nurses, four weeks, one clinic, and voluntary participation.
expectations.evidence: “In a voluntary four-week pilot at one clinic, 18 nurses used a scheduling tool”.

expectations.text: Preserves median weekly 46 to 39 minutes with no causal claim and explains no control plus concurrent staffing changes.
expectations.evidence: “median weekly scheduling time fell from 46 to 39 minutes”; “observed seven-minute reduction”; “no control group” and “concurrent staffing changes may explain part of it” prevent a causal claim.

expectations.text: States six of nine survey respondents preferred it rather than six of 18 or a majority of all nurses.
expectations.evidence: “Nine nurses completed the optional survey; six of those nine preferred the tool”; responses “cannot establish preference across the full group or other clinics.”

expectations.text: States patient safety was not measured; any next step is framed as recommendation, not a planned commitment.
expectations.evidence: “Patient safety was not measured”; “A next step is a controlled evaluation” recommends further work before a broader rollout decision.

expectations.text: 100–150 words in one paragraph without heading or bullets.
expectations.evidence: 112 whitespace-delimited words, one paragraph beginning “In a voluntary four-week pilot”, with no heading or bullets.

review_method: Independent single blind agent review; not human feedback
